subject: Embeddings model fit & POC plan — next steps and benchmarks
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeretail.com>, Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acmeretail.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings model fit & POC plan — next steps and benchmarks

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on the product search use case and the realities around seasonal catalog churn. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Objective: improve product search relevance and recommendation recall for long-tail SKUs while keeping embedding storage and compute predictable.
- Data: ~2M SKUs historically, but you want to validate on a 50k sample of active SKUs + 10k query logs.
- Constraints: PII redaction required, KMS for encryption at rest, SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Redwood recommended evaluation plan (high level)
- Lightweight POC (2 weeks): run candidate embedding models on your 50k sample + historical queries.
- Metrics we will measure: recall@10, MAP@10, MRR, and median cosine distance for known-good pairs. Targets we discussed: recall@10 >= 0.80 and MAP@10 >= 0.40 as an initial threshold to consider production; we'll refine after the first run.
- Candidate models to evaluate: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384d, low-cost baseline), open-quantized COGL-1B-emb (512d, good lexical+semantic), and a 1536d candidate (RWin-1.5B-emb) for head-tail separation.
- Dimensionality tradeoffs: 384d will be fastest/cost-efficient; 1536d tends to improve MAP for long-tail queries but increases storage and vector search latency. We'll provide concrete cost delta estimates for each.

Deliverables we will share after the POC
- Benchmark CSV with per-query metrics (recall@k, MAP, MRR) and sample failure cases (attached preview).
- Prompt set / evaluation queries we used and canonical relevance judgments (you can review and edit).
- Suggested embedding refresh cadence and drift-monitoring thresholds (recommend weekly drift checks initially).

Action items / timeline
1) You share the 50k SKU sample + 10k anonymized query logs (Sarah) — target: Wed 2026-04-01.
2) We spin the POC in a sandbox (Redwood hosted) and deliver results in ~10 business days after dataset receipt.
3) Parallel: procurement/security asks (SOC2, KMS, data handling) — we will loop in our compliance team.

Attachments: preview of benchmark CSV and a short prompt set we plan to use.

Questions for you now
- Does the recall@10 >= 0.80 / MAP@10 >= 0.40 initial threshold make sense as a go/no-go gate for the POC?
- Any blockers on providing the anonymized query logs by Wed 4/1?

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if you'd like to walk through the plan.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0123 | dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: acme_embeddings-benchmark.csv (CSV, 45KB)
Attachment: recommended-prompt-sets.txt (TXT, 6KB)
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeretail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acmeretail.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit & POC plan — next steps and benchmarks

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the detailed recap — this is exactly the kind of structure we wanted. A few clarifications from our side:

- The recall@10 >= 0.80 / MAP@10 >= 0.40 gate seems reasonable as a starting point. The product team will want to see distribution plots (not just averages) so we can understand head vs tail behavior.
- We can provide the 50k SKU sample and 10k anonymized query logs, but we need KMS-handling and SOC2 evidence before we transfer anything. Procurement asked for our SOC2 questionnaire answers too; I attached a short requirements PDF with the things they flagged.
- Also please include a simple estimate of delta storage + search latency for 384d vs 1536d vectors — our infra team will need that for cost modeling.

I'll aim to get the dataset to you by end of day Thu 2026-04-01 assuming procurement doesn't push back. If there are specific redaction steps you expect on our side, call them out.

Thanks,
Sarah Jenkins
Director of Product Analytics | Acme Retail
Attachment: acme_customer-requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Tom Lewis <tom.lewis@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit & POC plan — next steps and benchmarks

Thanks Sarah — appreciate the procurement note and the requirement doc. Two quick items:

1) Redaction guidance: please pseudonymize user identifiers and remove free-text customer notes that could contain PII. For product attributes (title, description, category) we just need raw text; prices/SKU IDs can remain. If you prefer, we can provide a short redaction script you can run locally — let me know.

2) Attached is a mini benchmark CSV (first-pass sample) and the exact prompt / query set we'll use for evaluation. Also included in the Drive link: a short notebook that computes recall@k, MAP@k, and a per-query delta table so you can see which items changed most.

Concrete POC plan (detailed)
- Week 0 (dataset hand-off): Receive dataset and security paperwork (KMS endpoint, SOC2 attestation).
- Days 1–3: Ingest + normalize, run candidate embedding models at small scale (all-MiniLM, COGL-1B-emb, RWin-1.5B-emb).
- Days 4–7: Run search experiments, compute metrics, generate failure-case bucket (5–10% lowest-performing queries).
- Day 8–10: Deliver report + short walkthrough with sample queries and recommended model.

Monitoring & drift recommendations
- Embed population-level drift: weekly cosine similarity distribution checks and automatic alerts for median shift > 0.06.
- Per-query degradation: track rolling 7-day MAP and flag queries with >15% drop from baseline.

Next steps I need from you
- Confirm dataset delivery timeline (Thu 4/1 works).
- Confirm procurement contact for SOC2/KMS so we can route evidence.

I'll also include Marissa on pricing and Dev on the technical KMS questions in a follow-up.

Best,
Dylan

Attachment: acme_embeddings-mini-benchmark.csv (CSV, 12KB)
Attachment: recommended-prompt-sets.txt (TXT, 6KB)

Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Embeddings model fit & POC plan — next steps and benchmarks

Marissa / Dev — forwarding the Acme thread and attachments (see above). Quick asks so we can move fast if the POC looks good: 

Marissa (pricing)
- Please prepare a 3-tier pricing stub for the POC -> pilot -> dedicated options. Include estimated monthly cost deltas for 384d vs 1536d at our standard vector-store pricing assumptions. Use ACME-2026-055 as the deal id.

Dev (security/ops)
- Can you confirm what evidence we can produce for KMS integration (we typically provide KMS flow doc + contact for a short kick-off). Also flag any SOC2 gaps we should expect when sharing the initial sample.

Background notes:
- Sarah asked specifically for distribution plots (head vs tail) in the final deliverable — we should include both per-query histograms and percentile tables.
- Recommended initial guardrails: recall@10 >= 0.80 + weekly drift monitoring; early rollback policy if weekly median cosine shift > 0.08.

Pls reply-all with any missing asks — I'd like to get pricing/ops answers back to Sarah by EOD Mon 2026-04-05.

Thanks,
Dylan
